text:
Seattle trailed for most of the night and still had the game tied until the 17th minute of the third, when Leon Draisaitl snapped one home to make it 2-1 at 17:33. Connor McDavid added an empty-looking insurance goal 82 seconds later, a wrist shot that carried a 37 percent chance of scoring. Edmonton won 3-1, and the scoreboard barely captured how lopsided the play was.

The Oilers piled up 62 shot attempts to Seattle's 38 and out-chanced the Kraken 4.0 expected goals to 1.71. By the quality of their chances, they deserved to win 82 percent of the time. Edmonton's best stretches came in the first and third periods, when they generated 1.59 and 2.04 expected goals against 0.14 and 0.36 for Seattle. Owen Michaels opened the scoring at 2:51 of the first, a shot that rated only 4 percent, a reminder that goals can arrive from modest looks. McDavid and Draisaitl were the engine, each finishing above 2.6 expected goals for while their lines gave up almost nothing. Draisaitl put six shots on net.

Seattle's only real push was the second period, when they outchanced Edmonton 1.21 to 0.37. Bobby McMann converted a power play wrist shot at 9:06 to tie it at 1-1. Philipp Grubauer kept the Kraken in it, stopping 23 of 25 against 3.63 expected goals against, which is about 1.6 goals better than average. Devon Levi stopped 25 of 26 for Edmonton and earned first star, but the Oilers' skaters did most of the work in front of him.
